boundaries.evidence: Definition: both expectation and almost-sure conclusion quantify over every θ; when Θ is empty both are vacuous, so the completeness condition holds for any supplied statistic.
Definition: g=0 satisfies integrability, zero expectation and the almost-sure conclusion under every member; no division by an expectation occurs.
Definition: for a singleton parameter family the same implication still ranges over every integrable g; singleton family does not automatically imply completeness.
Definition: when T is constant under every law, zero expectation of the constant g(T) forces its almost-sure zero value; only the stated integrability implication is required.

boundaries.reason: Completeness quantifies over arbitrary parameter labels and integrable functions, not an ordered interval with boundary points.
The complete-statistic condition evaluates a supplied measurable T and every eligible g; it selects neither a parameter nor a representative.
Completeness is introduced by a one-direction zero-mean implication, not a separate biconditional proposition.
No converse of the defining completeness implication is asserted as an additional result.

boundaries.evidence: Definition: Ω is an arbitrary subset of H, so Ω=∅ gives an empty associated family; the separate full-rank condition requires a nonempty open subset and then fails.
Definition: H={η:0<Z(η)<∞} excludes Z=0 before A=log Z is used; h may vanish pointwise and those density values are zero.
Definition: pη=h exp(η·T−A(η)) with A=log Z integrates to Z/Z=1 for each η∈Ω; Ω may also be a singleton without being full-rank in positive dimension.
Definition: the condition that no b≠0 has b·T=c on {h>0} expressly excludes redundant displayed coordinates from full rank, while the exponential-family density itself permits them.
Definition: Z=0 and Z=∞ are excluded by the strict conditions defining H; no density or log-normalizer at either integral endpoint is promised.
Definition: full rank expressly requires Ω to contain a nonempty open subset, whereas the family construction uses supplied h,T,μ and Ω and chooses no η.

boundaries.reason: The density representation and the separate full-rank convention are definitions; the item asserts no equivalence theorem to prove forward.
No converse theorem recovering an exponential-family representation from a statistic property appears in this definition.

boundaries.evidence: Definition: for Θ=∅ the integral identities are vacuous, and the bounded common witness vu=0 exists for every bounded u. Then the family-null ideal is all A; A△∅ belongs to it, so containment modulo that ideal is vacuous.
Definition: the test function u=0 admits vu=0 in every candidate sigma-field; zero family probabilities enter only the explicitly defined family-null ideal.
Definition: u=1 admits vu=1 and preserves the displayed integral identities; no normalization by a possibly zero event probability is used.
Definition: family-null differences are handled by A△B∈N, so null-set degeneracy changes equality only modulo the explicitly specified ideal.

boundaries.reason: Minimal sufficient sigma-field containment is a relation between sigma-fields modulo an ideal, with no numerical interval endpoint.
The definition requires an existing sufficient Gstar and quantified bounded witnesses vu; it proves no existence or selection of a minimal field.
The integral identity characterizes sufficiency by definition, and minimality is a universal containment requirement; no iff theorem is claimed.
The definition does not assert a converse construction of Gstar from containment alone without its stated sufficiency requirement.

boundaries.evidence: Definition: Θ is a subset of R in an experiment and no nonemptiness is imposed; when Θ is empty there are no ordered pairs θ1<θ2 and the MLR pair requirement is vacuous.
Definition: R=pθ2/pθ1 on {pθ1>0}; numerator zero gives ratio zero, pθ1=0<pθ2 gives +∞, and both-zero points are excluded by U={pθ1+pθ2>0}.

Definition: for a singleton Θ no ordered parameter pair exists; if two selected densities agree their ratio is one μ-almost everywhere on U, represented by the constant Borel nondecreasing function one.
Definition: identical laws have equal selected RN densities μ-almost everywhere for each fixed pair, so the constant ratio case is covered without a common null set across all pairs.

boundaries.reason: MLR compares any two labels θ1<θ2 in Θ; it imposes no openness, interval boundary, or value of a ratio at a missing endpoint label.

boundaries.evidence: Definition: Assume AC and the sentence Choose the simultaneous finite-valued nonnegative density representatives identify the only version-selection use; no simultaneous common exceptional null set is claimed.

boundaries.reason: MLR in T is a pairwise representation convention, not an iff theorem between MLR and sufficiency; the Definition expressly says T need not be sufficient.
No reverse implication from a test property or sufficiency to MLR is asserted in this item.

boundaries.evidence: Definition: the relation is defined for θ,η∈Θ; when Θ=∅ there are no such pairs and the relation has no equivalence classes.

boundaries.reason: Observational equivalence uses equality of probability laws on events; parameter labels have no distinguished numeric zero.

boundaries.evidence: Definition: on a one-label model θ=η is permitted, since No distinctness ... is required and Pθ=Pθ.
Definition: distinct parameter labels with identical sampling laws satisfy Pθ=Pη; injectivity is not required.

boundaries.reason: The parameter map in this definition has an arbitrary domain with no order or interval boundary assumed.

boundaries.evidence: Definition: θ∼η is determined by Pθ=Pη and selects no representative of an equivalence class.
Definition: if θ∼η then the defining if and only if clause gives Pθ=Pη, hence equality on every A∈A.
Definition: if Pθ(A)=Pη(A) for every measurable event, the laws are equal and the same defining if and only if clause gives θ∼η.
Definition: on Θ=∅ the parameterwise probability-section and eventwise measurability clauses are vacuous and all parameter preimages are empty.
Definition: each A↦K(θ,A) is a probability measure, so its value on ∅ is zero; zero belongs to the stated [0,1] codomain.
Definition: each section is a probability measure on X, so K(θ,X)=1; the required endpoint value lies in [0,1].
Definition: K(θ,A)=Pθ(A) requires equality to the experiment law, with no injectivity requirement on θ; equal laws may give identical sections.
Definition: the event-probability codomain is [0,1] and its relative Borel sigma-algebra explicitly includes both endpoints, so maps attaining zero or one are allowed.
Definition: K is a supplied function satisfying section and measurability clauses; representation means specified equality, not an arbitrary section-selection principle.
Definition: The kernel represents the given experiment exactly when K(θ,A)=Pθ(A); thus representation entails that equality for every θ and A.

Definition: a kernel satisfying K(θ,A)=Pθ(A) for every θ and A represents the given experiment by the same exactly when clause; arbitrary experiments are not asserted to satisfy the kernel measurability condition.
Definition: the score is defined at a fixed θ∈Θ where selected densities are differentiable; Θ=∅ supplies no such θ, so it defines no score or information value there.
Definition: Sθ=0 is explicitly assigned on {pθ=0}, a Pθ-null set; a score zero almost surely has I(θ)=Eθ[Sθ²]=0.
Definition: d=1 is explicitly the scalar derivative ∂θ log pθ; the displayed scalar second moment includes an information value one when that second moment equals one.
Definition: parameter-constant differentiable density representatives have zero derivatives on {pθ>0}, and the explicit extension elsewhere gives score zero and information zero.
Definition: Θ is open in Rd and derivatives are required at a specified θ∈Θ, so boundary labels outside Θ are not assigned scores; scalar I lies in [0,+∞], allowing zero and infinite information.
Definition: simultaneous selection of the arbitrary-index RN density family explicitly uses AC and is relative to specified differentiable representatives.

boundaries.reason: Score and Fisher information are defined by derivatives and expectations, not by a biconditional theorem.
No converse theorem deriving parameter differentiability from the existence of a second-moment matrix is asserted.

boundaries.evidence: Statement: independence is asserted under every Pθ, so with an empty parameter family there is no law requiring verification. With a nonempty family, steps 1.1–3.1 apply separately under each supplied law.
Step 2.1: gC=qC−pC is bounded even when the ancillary probability pC=0; completeness makes qC(T)=0 almost surely and step 3.1 factors the joint probability.
Step 2.1: the identical bounded-function argument allows pC=1, and step 3.1 gives joint probability Pθ(T∈D) when the ancillary event has probability one.
Steps 1.1–3.1: if U is constant, each pC is zero or one and the same conditional event calculation proves independence; no nondegeneracy hypothesis is used.

boundaries.reason: Basu Statement imposes no interval structure on parameter labels; the only probability endpoints are covered in the zero and one rows.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.1: C is an arbitrary supplied Borel event; the kernel K already exists by sufficiency F1. Step 2.1 uses the common ancillary probability under each law, not a new family of selected versions.

boundaries.reason: The Basu Statement is the implication complete sufficient T and ancillary U implies independence, not an equivalence with those hypotheses.
Independence is not asserted to imply completeness, sufficiency, or ancillarity; the theorem has no reverse claim.

boundaries.evidence: Statement: Ω≠∅ is an explicit hypothesis; step 1.1 fixes η0∈Ω. Thus an empty parameter family is excluded before forming the reference probability.
Step 1.1: every density is positive exactly on {h>0}; the RN density ratio is asserted only Pη0-almost surely, so h=0 points require no zero-over-zero division.
Step 1.1: at η=η0 the exponential RN ratio is exp(0)=1; step 2.1 then still applies the common-reference criterion, including a singleton Ω.

Statement and step 1.1: sufficiency requires no rank or nonredundancy condition beyond the density representation; even constant canonical coordinates yield a Borel exponential RN ratio and step 2.1 establishes sufficiency.
F1 and Definition of exponential family: η∈Ω⊆H requires 0<Z(η)<∞, so neither normalization endpoint Z=0 nor Z=∞ occurs; step 1.1 uses the finite A(η) differences.
Step 1.1: Fix any η0∈Ω is justified by explicit nonemptiness and is one reference selection. A1 and step 2.1 record AC through the common-reference factorization supplier.

boundaries.reason: The Statement asserts exponential-family canonical-statistic sufficiency only; it does not state an iff characterization of all sufficient statistics.
No converse representation of a family as exponential from sufficiency of T is claimed in this theorem.
